title: Linearity of maps between transported etale module objects
statement: Let U,V,f,O,L,La,Lr,er,ea be as in [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-module-object], except that no ring adjunction or compatibility of adjunction hom equivalences is required. Suppose H assigns an Lr(O)-module sheaf to each O-module sheaf G [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], with abelian isomorphisms dG: FU(HG) ≅ La(FV(G)). Assume actual source and target scalar-action morphisms satisfying the product-comparison transport identity for every G. Then for each O-linear sheaf map phi:G → G', the abelian map g = dG followed by La(FV(phi)) followed by dG'^(-1) is sectionwise Lr(O)-linear: g_W(r • m) = r • g_W(m). This asserts only linearity of a given abelian map; it assumes the objects and their transported actions rather than constructing them.

proof.text: Check the source action square on sections using the actual scalar-action formulas and the linearity of phi; it is an equality of sheaf morphisms.

Obtain finite-product preservation of L from the algebraic-structures theorem. Apply L to the source square, substitute the two transport identities, and use naturality of ea and prodComparison. The private transport_action_square calculation cancels the invertible product and object comparisons to obtain the target action square.

The evaluation functor preserves binary products. BinaryFan.IsLimit.lift supplies a product section with projections (r,m). Evaluate the target action square there, substitute the action formulas, and obtain the required scalar linearity.
